text.label: Heading: Reviews are not vanity.
text.value: Clients work with companies that have the most reviews

text.label: Text: They are your entry fee.
text.value: not who does the best work!

text.label: Text: Before anyone calls you, they read about you…
text.value: That is how people decide now. They pull up Google, look at who has the most stars and the most reviews, and call them. If you have eleven reviews and they have two hundred, you were never in the running, and it has nothing to do with who does better work. So we build the thing that asks for you. Every customer you work with gets checked on while the job is still going — a short survey, at the points that matter, asking how it is going. You find out somebody is unhappy while you can still pick up the phone and fix it, instead of reading it on Google on Saturday. And when a customer tells you they are happy, that is the moment they are asked to say so publicly — on Google, on Yelp, wherever people look you up. Every customer, every time, forever, without anyone remembering to do it.

props.intro: Automated Five Star Reviews is one of five systems we build. They are designed to connect, so a customer is never dropped between them.

props.text: The ask goes out while they are still happy.
Not three days later when somebody remembers. The moment the job is marked done, the message is already gone.

props.caption: An illustration of the flow, not a customer's real thread. Nobody on your team has to remember to send it, and nobody has to feel awkward asking.

messages.text: Hi Dana — glad we got that taken care of today. If we did right by you, would you mind leaving a quick review? Takes about thirty seconds.
Happy to. Send me the link?
Right here — thank you, it genuinely helps a small business like ours.

props.text: And then they belong on your own website.

Now the part nobody thinks about. You earned those reviews. Right now they live on a page that also lists the three competitors nearest you — so the star rating you worked years for is doing its selling inside somebody else's shopping list.
Your rating sits beside theirs, with distance and hours and a map. The customer is comparing. That is what the page is built to make them do.
The same reviews, pulled in and kept current, with nobody else on the screen — next to your work, your prices and a button that books you. Nothing to compare against.
Both, ideally. The profile is how they find you. Your site is where the reviews finish the job.
